lesson.title: Improving completed human work
lesson.summary: Test improvement of genuinely completed human work rather than replacement of an unfinished judgment.

prerequisites.reason: Completed human work does not bypass the gateway or its decision-influence analysis.

blocks: The **completed-human-work condition** concerns AI intended to improve the result of a human activity already completed. Identify that earlier activity and its completed result.
Do not treat a blank form or an unfinished recommendation as completed human assessment. Completion is a factual requirement, not a synonym for 'a person is somewhere in the process'.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(b), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Fictional Northbridge: a person has completed a written report; a tool corrects spelling without changing findings. The case illustrates an improvement-of-completed-work hypothesis.
The actual function and effects still require the gateway and profiling checks. This example is not a guarantee that every writing assistant satisfies a derogation in every listed context.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(b), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Changed case: before the person has evaluated an applicant, the tool supplies the substantive suitability recommendation. That is different from improving a completed result.
Changed case: the tool rewrites a completed finding and alters its meaning. Assess whether the claimed improvement now materially influences the decision or creates significant risk.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(b), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: The record should identify the completed activity, the allowed changes, the person reviewing them and the effect on conclusions. Retain before/after evidence appropriate to the case.
A contract saying 'editing only' does not answer whether the system actually changes findings. Apply the full paragraph 3 test to the demonstrated operation.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(b), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

questions.prompt: What must be identified for the completed-human-work condition?

options.blocks: A previously completed human activity and result
options.reason: The condition expressly requires completion before improvement.

options.blocks: Only any human in the organisation
options.reason: General human presence does not establish prior completion.
An unfinished assessment is not a completed result.

questions.prompt: A tool corrects spelling in a completed report, then adds a new adverse finding. What should happen?

options.blocks: Ignore findings because spelling is also corrected
options.reason: A cosmetic function cannot erase the substantive change.
Edits can affect conclusions and harm risks.

options.blocks: Reassess the actual change and decision influence
options.reason: The full condition and gateway depend on actual effects.
